nodes.label: XenoDesk
nodes.rationale: Multi-tenant business workspace combining Sourcing Workspace, Customer Genome, Creator Commerce and Agent Workspace; modules share identity, permissions, messaging, scheduling, realtime events, audit logging, AI retrieval, and a common tenant boundary.

nodes.label: Realtime Events
nodes.rationale: Published by business with monotonically increasing IDs through Redis, exposed via SSE; short replay windows; clients resume via Last-Event-ID and refetch on gaps.

nodes.label: Audit Logging
nodes.rationale: Audit records for business-sensitive actions such as exports, consent changes, identity links, role changes.

nodes.label: AI Retrieval
nodes.rationale: Hybrid retrieval: tenant-bound vector search plus PostgreSQL full-text search, reciprocal rank fusion, minimum score; retrieved chunks hydrated from PostgreSQL under RLS.

nodes.label: modular monolith
nodes.rationale: One FastAPI application is the API; feature modules are separated into routers, models, and domain services; keeps deployment and transactions simple while preserving boundaries for later extraction.

nodes.label: polyglot persistence
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL is the only system of record; vectors sit behind the VectorStore interface (pgvector default, Qdrant optional); MongoDB stores high-volume loosely structured non-authoritative documents; Redis provides queue, cache, pub-sub or streams, and rate-limit primitives; Ollama serves the local LLM and embedding models.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL
nodes.rationale: System of record: identities, memberships, orders, consent, outbox, idempotency keys, jobs, and audit records live only there.

nodes.label: VectorStore
nodes.rationale: Interface in platform/vector/ with upsert, search, and delete operations that always require tenant context; pgvector and Qdrant implementations.

nodes.label: Qdrant
nodes.rationale: Optional drop-in vector database chosen when measured scale or latency requires it; search returns chunk IDs and scores, text re-hydrated from PostgreSQL under RLS.

nodes.label: MongoDB
nodes.rationale: High-volume, loosely structured, non-authoritative documents via tenant-scoped repositories: raw webhook payloads, sourcing snapshots, ads snapshots, agent traces; not the source of truth for business state.

nodes.label: Redis
nodes.rationale: Queue, cache, pub-sub or streams, and rate-limit primitives.

nodes.label: Ollama
nodes.rationale: Local LLM and embedding model as a replaceable, stateless inference service.

nodes.label: Next.js
nodes.rationale: Browser workspace with React app shell and persistent navigation.

nodes.label: Authentication
nodes.rationale: Bearer access tokens validated; JWT decoded and validated, user resolved from PostgreSQL, account status and token revocation checked, active business membership resolved, role loaded from the membership record; roles evaluated at request time.

nodes.label: RBAC
nodes.rationale: Role-based access control; role checks at the API boundary.

nodes.label: token policy
nodes.rationale: Access tokens short-lived; refresh tokens rotated on every use with reuse detection that revokes the whole family; browser storage prefers httpOnly, Secure, SameSite refresh cookies.

nodes.label: business_id
nodes.rationale: Derived from the authenticated principal; required column on every tenant-scoped operation; clients must not choose a tenant by placing business_id in request bodies; X-Business-Id selects the membership after authorization.

nodes.label: Row Level Security
nodes.rationale: SET LOCAL app.business_id inside each transaction so pooled connections never carry tenant state between requests; application connects as a non-owner role with FORCE RLS on tenant tables, including embedding tables.

nodes.label: JSONB
nodes.rationale: Semi-structured data that belongs to a transactional record uses JSONB columns before a separate store is considered.

nodes.label: SQLAlchemy
nodes.rationale: Asynchronous sessions for API access.

nodes.label: Alembic
nodes.rationale: Versioned migrations; migration role runs CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector.

nodes.label: idempotency keys
nodes.rationale: Provider inbound event IDs, outbound message identities, review requests per order, consent records per review, scheduled jobs, embedding jobs per source record and content hash.

nodes.label: outbox pattern
nodes.rationale: Business transaction commits domain change and pending outbound row together; dispatcher claims with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED; preserves ordering per recipient, retries with bounded exponential backoff, moves exhausted rows to dead-letter state for owner or operator review.

nodes.label: feature routers
nodes.rationale: Own transport concerns, delegate business rules to domain/platform code; feature boundaries: auth, sourcing, genome, reviews, ads, workspace, events, webhooks.

nodes.label: request pipeline
nodes.rationale: CORS, context middleware, idempotency, authentication, principal and role resolution, tenant-bound session, feature router, domain/platform service, stores.

nodes.label: embedding job
nodes.rationale: Source row created or updated, enqueue embedding job (unique on source_id and content_hash), chunk, embed via Ollama, upsert chunk rows in PostgreSQL and vectors in the VectorStore under the owning business_id, publish index updated event; always runs in background workers, never inline in an API request.

nodes.label: embedding_documents
nodes.rationale: One row per indexed source record: id, business_id, source_type, source_id, content_hash, embedding_model, status.

nodes.label: embedding_chunks
nodes.rationale: Chunk text and metadata: id, business_id, document_id, chunk_index, content, metadata jsonb, and embedding vector(N) (populated in pgvector mode only).

nodes.label: HNSW cosine index
nodes.rationale: HNSW cosine index on embedding_chunks with a btree on business_id; RLS applies to similarity search automatically.

nodes.label: documents repositories
nodes.rationale: Tenant-scoped MongoDB repositories in platform/documents/ (the only code that touches Mongo); async driver such as Motor; inject the tenant filter into every query; raw handles not exported to feature code.

nodes.label: webhook_payloads
nodes.rationale: Full raw provider payloads keyed by provider event ID, for debugging and replay analysis; TTL configurable.

nodes.label: sourcing_snapshots
nodes.rationale: Imported or scraped supplier product data with variable schema; replaced on refresh.

nodes.label: ads_snapshots
nodes.rationale: Large nested ads intelligence documents; TTL or latest-N per source.

nodes.label: agent_traces
nodes.rationale: Agent conversation transcripts, retrieval results, prompts, and model usage detail.

nodes.label: design invariants
nodes.rationale: 17 design invariants: PostgreSQL only system of record; no tenant-scoped query without verified context; no outbound message without persisted authorized eligible outbound record; no webhook processed twice for the same event; no automatic restock notification bypassing owner approval; no AI tool can mutate business data; no vector search without tenant context; embeddings always scoped by business_id; retrieved text is data, never instructions; LLM unavailability never breaks non-AI features; secondary-store outage never fails business transaction or webhook acknowledgement; erasure and retention policies cover every store holding personal data.

nodes.label: graceful AI degradation
nodes.rationale: LLM and embedding calls have timeouts, bounded retries, and a concurrency limit; when Ollama is down, slow or saturated, the agent answers from FAQ matches and allow-listed read-only data intents, or returns an explicit AI unavailable response; embedding jobs that fail are retried with backoff and recorded; they never block the business transaction that created the source record.

nodes.label: hybrid search
nodes.rationale: Vector similarity combined with PostgreSQL full-text search via reciprocal rank fusion; improves recall for product names, SKUs and Bangla-English queries where embeddings alone miss exact matches.

nodes.label: prompt-injection resistance
nodes.rationale: Retrieved reviews, customer text and ad copy are untrusted data in delimited blocks; the system prompt states the block is data, never instructions; read-only allow-listed tools with tenant and role checks on every invocation; no tool permission changes from data.

nodes.label: Secondary Store Projection
nodes.rationale: Committed change in PostgreSQL, projection job, write to vector store or MongoDB, status recorded, reconciliation job detects and repairs drift; secondary-store outage never fails business transaction or webhook acknowledgement.

nodes.label: erasure workflow
nodes.rationale: A single erasure workflow removes a data subject's records from PostgreSQL, vectors, MongoDB documents, and object storage, and writes an audit record; retention periods defined per data class, enforced by TTL indexes and scheduled jobs.

nodes.label: Agent service
nodes.rationale: Retrieve, prompt and validate; feature routers never call Ollama, the vector store or MongoDB directly.

nodes.label: SSE authentication
nodes.rationale: Native EventSource cannot send an Authorization header, so the realtime client uses a fetch-based SSE client or a single-use stream ticket passed as a query parameter.

nodes.label: API service
nodes.rationale: API service (Python, FastAPI): typed request and response models, async I/O for webhooks and SSE, Pydantic validation at the boundary.

nodes.label: Database
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL: row-level tenant scoping, strong constraints for idempotency keys, JSONB for flexible snapshot payloads, mature advisory locking for restock detection.

nodes.label: Queue and Cache
nodes.rationale: Redis plus Celery or Dramatiq: delayed jobs (review requests), batch sends, bounded retries, cache for hot read endpoints.

nodes.label: Server-Sent Events
nodes.rationale: Server-Sent Events: one-way server to client push; simpler than WebSockets and survives proxies; auto-reconnect.

nodes.label: Frontend
nodes.rationale: React with Next.js: app shell with persistent sidebar, per-page routes for the SSE stream to survive navigation, server components for initial reads.

nodes.label: Object Storage
nodes.rationale: S3-compatible: CSV imports, uploaded screenshots, export artifacts.

nodes.label: LLMPort
nodes.rationale: Provider-agnostic client behind a LLMPort interface so the model can change without touching feature code.

nodes.label: Alembic
nodes.rationale: Versioned, reversible schema migrations.

nodes.label: Identity and Consent
nodes.rationale: Messaging identity links, contact permissions, opt-outs and consent records. Used by bubbles, Restore Product and Review.

nodes.label: Messaging Gateway
nodes.rationale: Inbound: webhook signature check, idempotent event store. Outbound: channel adapters (Email, SMS, Messenger, WhatsApp), send-time eligibility, rate limits, bounded retries, one delivery log for all purposes.

nodes.label: Scheduler and Queue
nodes.rationale: Delayed jobs (review requests), batch sends (retries), restock detection.

nodes.label: Audit log
nodes.rationale: Batch approvals, exports, consent changes, identity links, role changes.

nodes.label: CustomerOrderSource
nodes.rationale: Pluggable adapter interface isolating the platform from the authoritative source of customers, orders and inventory.

nodes.label: Restore Product
nodes.rationale: Restock detection to restock events plus owner dashboard notification; no message is sent automatically.

nodes.label: review_replies
nodes.rationale: Verbatim text, message_id, received_at, channel, customer, order and product, written once; insert-only, no update on the text columns.

nodes.label: marketing card
nodes.rationale: Generated from review_replies verbatim text (exact string, no rewriting); labelled Customer review; must not imitate Messenger or WhatsApp UI chrome.

nodes.label: Read-only tools allowlist
nodes.rationale: Static allow-list of read-only functions; no dynamic tool registration path; tool calls re-authorized for tenant and role on every invocation.

nodes.label: API conventions
nodes.rationale: Base path /api for product APIs, /webhooks for callbacks; versioning /api/v1; OAuth2 bearer auth; business_id from token; cursor pagination; ISO-8601 UTC; Idempotency-Key; optimistic locking via version column.

nodes.label: Open Technical Decisions
nodes.rationale: 13 decisions (OD-01 to OD-13) with options and current defaults; impacts on requirements recorded per decision.

nodes.label: Idempotency
nodes.rationale: Unique constraints on inbound event IDs and outbound idempotency keys; mutating sends accept Idempotency-Key; replays return original result with Idempotent-Replay: true.

nodes.label: Rate limiting
nodes.rationale: Per tenant per endpoint; send endpoints additionally limited per channel.

nodes.label: No fabricated data
nodes.rationale: The API returns explicit null plus a reason enum (not_visible, not_available, not_tracked, unresolved) rather than defaults; UI renders a dedicated unavailable component.

nodes.label: Least data to AI
nodes.rationale: Redaction layer strips or masks personal fields before the prompt is assembled; the LLM port receives only an allow-listed payload.

nodes.label: Time
nodes.rationale: Store UTC (timestamptz). Display in the business timezone, resolved per business timezone setting. Scheduled jobs compute due times in business time and persist the resolved UTC instant.

nodes.label: Untrusted input
nodes.rationale: Ad copy, review text and customer messages are stored and displayed as data, never interpolated into system prompts or tool schemas.
